newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses mixed, Wall St boosts some.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses mixed, Wall St boosts some.

text.p: European stocks made a mixed start on Thursday with many investors encouraged by New York, where demand for technology shares pushed Wall Street to a firm close.

On currency markets, the dollar strengthened against the mark, Swiss franc and Japanese yen ahead of a German central bank meeting on Thursday, although the Bundesbank was not expected to change interest rates.
Shares in London and Paris saw the biggest rises in early deals, enlivened by merger and bid activity. But Frankfurt floor trade slipped in thin volumes ahead of the holiday period.
London climbed 0.2 percent with trading buoyed by bids and share buybacks in the market over the last two days which have totalled 2.5 billion pounds ($4.2 billion).

Wall Street also continued to underpin market sentiment. The Dow Jones industrial average put on another 38 points overnight to 6,346 in an end-of-year rush to snap up technology stocks, adding to Tuesday's 40 point rally.
"You can see by the volume and general breadth of the improvement yesterday that there are quite a few people who feel sufficiently strongly enough to want to get into this market," one dealer said.
Paris moved ahead 0.8 percent, the best showing of the morning in Europe. The market was cheered by New York and a flurry of merger-related announcements in the pharmaceuticals and retail sectors.
Elf Aquitaine and Sanofi rose strongly after Elf said it would be desirable for its pharmaceutical unit Sanofi to merge with other laboratories to boost profitability.
Rhone-Poulenc climbed 0.6 percent to 167 francs. The drugs group is merging its animal health business with Merck to create a venture with 8.5 billion francs ($1.6 billion) in annual sales.

In Frankfurt, stocks fell as the policy-making council of the Bundesbank met to set its money supply target for 1997. Economists saw little chance that the decision would be accompanied by an interest rate cut.
On the currency front, the dollar was stronger after a sharp drop in Japanese stocks overnight and because of a degree of uncertainty over the Bundesbank meeting.

Though most traders believed German interest rates would not be changed, some said an outside chance remained that the bank would fix its key securities repurchase rate slightly lower over the year-end holiday period.
The yen weakened as a 2.6 percent drop in the Nikkei 225 index of Japanese stocks overnight was seen arguing for Japanese interest rates to remain at record lows for now.
The U.S. currency climbed to 1.5583 marks at one stage before slipping back but remained well above the level of 1.5541 in late trade on Wednesday.

"It looks like there's been a return to the generalised dollar/Europe play again this morning on the off-chance the Bundesbank may come up with something," said Joe Prendergast, currency strategist at Merrill Lynch in London.
The Swiss franc was lower in Europe, meantime, and set a two-year low at 1.3372 per dollar and a three-year low at 85.82 centimes per mark.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5569 marks and 114.10 yen, compared with 1.5541 and 113.65 in late business on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 7.7 points at 4,025.5.
In Frankfurt, the 30-share DAX was 14.99 lower at 2,231.68.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 12.82 at 2,231.82.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $369.60 an ounce, compared to Wednesday's close of $369.10. Silver was at $4.87, up one cent.
